key_insight: In a multi-step coding setting, the researchers identify signals for an LLM’s next sub-goal in the outputs of a small set of attention heads. This suggests that intermediate goals can be localized within the model’s internal activity.
problem_solved: How can we determine whether LLMs internally represent goals that guide their actions, rather than merely generating plausible next steps?
method: Construct a coding environment with multiple sub-tasks to evaluate goal-seeking behavior and sub-goal selection.
Analyze attention-head outputs to locate internal representations of the next sub-goal.
Identify a sparse set of heads carrying sub-goal information.
impact: Locating sub-goal signals could help practitioners interpret how LLMs organize multi-step work and diagnose planning failures. The supplied abstract is truncated, so broader claims about prediction or control cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Task tree showing an overall coding goal branching into sub-goals and alternative execution paths.
Transformer diagram highlighting the small set of attention heads encoding the next sub-goal.
Timeline linking internal sub-goal signals to subsequent coding actions.
Conceptual heatmap illustrating concentrated sub-goal information across attention heads.
paper_authors: Arnab Sen Sharma, Eric Todd, Sheridan Feucht, Andy Arditi, Rohit Gandikota
